statement: Five teams of three students meet at a tournament. Each student shakes hands exactly once with every student from the other teams, but not with their own teammates. How many handshakes take place?

choices.misconception: I treated each team as a single person and counted handshakes between teams.
I took the 105 handshakes among all 15 students and removed 6 per team, counting each teammate pair twice.
I counted handshakes among all 15 students and forgot that teammates do not shake hands.
I counted 15 students times 12 handshakes each and forgot that every handshake involves two people.

hints: How many hands does one student shake?
Each student shakes hands with everyone outside their own team. Count per student, multiply by the number of students, then remember that each handshake was counted from both sides.
Each of the 15 students shakes 12 hands, giving 15 x 12 = 180, with every handshake counted twice.

solutions.reliable: Each student shakes hands with the 12 students in the other four teams. Counting from every student gives 15 x 12 = 180, but each handshake is counted by both people in it, so there are 180 / 2 = 90 handshakes. The transferable idea: counting from each person counts every pair twice, so halve.
solutions.elegant: All 15 students together would make 15 x 14 / 2 = 105 handshakes. Each team removes its 3 teammate pairs, so 105 - 5 x 3 = 90.

whyOnTest: Handshake counts test the count-then-halve idea; excluding teammates checks that you know exactly which pairs you are removing.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
